I am 66 years old and have farmed these fields since I was a young man. I never went to school, but I know this land. Every year I grow winter wheat and summer corn — that is what we do here in Quzhou. I have about 6 mu of land, and I put all of it into wheat in the autumn, then plant corn right after the wheat comes off in early June. There is barely a week between harvest and planting, so I cannot plough for the corn — I just drill the seeds straight into the wheat stubble, same as everyone else in the village. For wheat, I rotary-till before sowing.

I buy improved wheat seed from the shop in town — not the most expensive kind, but the one I have used for years and know it works. For corn, I always buy hybrid seed. My neighbor tried saving his own corn seed once and the yield was terrible, so I never do that.

For fertilizer, I think in bags, not kilograms. I put down about one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu for wheat before planting, and then topdress with urea at green-up and again at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. I do roughly the same for corn — one bag of compound at planting, then urea when the plants are knee-high. I know I probably use a bit more than I need, but I would rather waste a little money than lose half my crop. My son helps me calculate how many bags to buy now, but I decide based on what the fields look like.

I irrigate four times for wheat — overwinter water, green-up water, jointing water, and one more when the heads are filling. For corn I irrigate twice, at tasseling and grain-filling. Water costs money to pump, but without it nothing grows here on the North China Plain.

I spray herbicide once on each crop, and fungicide on wheat when I see rust. Maybe one insecticide spray if the worms come. That is usually three sprays on wheat and two on corn.

Last year I got about 420 kg of wheat per mu and 500 kg of corn per mu. If the weather is normal this year, I expect about the same. I am too old to try new crops or fancy methods. Wheat and corn have a buyer every year, and my family needs the grain and the cash. That is my plan.
